title: night-c-fine-detail
summary: Fine water detail from three tiling slope maps (fine chop, ripples, capillary), a Ripples sea group that gusts act on, a 1.5 m wavelength floor for wind-sea components, and a fix for the faceted, rectangular sun. Builds on night-b-roller-jitter.
problem: Fine visual detail was a few centimetres square at a few metres, and the sea looked spiky below about 10 km of fetch: waves under a metre cannot be held by the water mesh, and as components they printed hard glitter. Gusts changed almost nothing you could see. The sun was drawn rectangular.
implemented: Three fine-detail layers in the water shader: fine chop (35 cm to 1.5 m), ripples (5 to 35 cm) and capillary (1 to 5 cm). Each is a tiling slope map baked at start-up (inverse FFT, equal slope per octave), drifts with the wind, is looked at twice at different scales so it does not repeat, and fades out per pixel as a pixel grows to its shortest wavelength. What a layer carried when it fades becomes roughness in the glitter lobe.

How much slope the layers carry follows the wind (Cox and Munk total mean square slope) minus what the wave components already hold; "Amount" scales it. Display only: the physics and the boat never see it.

New Ripples sea group (Wind category): wind, direction, amount, gust response, stretch across the wind, and a mix for each layer. Auto adds one from the lead wind; a model without one follows its strongest wind sea. Zones and time windows apply to it. Only the strongest enabled Ripples group is drawn.
Gusts now roughen the ripples and lulls leave the water glassy (gust response, default 1). Patches 280 m across travel at 0.9 of the wind.
Wind sea and chop components stop at 1.5 m wavelength at any fetch; the rest of their slope is in the layers.

The sky sphere now normalises its direction per pixel. Before, the sun was bright only near a vertex of the 32 x 16 sphere and about 30 times dimmer at the centre of a facet, so its shape followed the facets.
The sun is the right size: a disc 0.53 degrees across with a soft edge, a close glare of about 0.8 degrees and a faint wide haze. It was a saturated blob about 8 degrees across.
Settings: "Ripples and fine detail (0 = off)" scales the layers. `?layers=0` brings back the old value-noise ripples for comparison.
Optional highlight shoulder in the water shader (`?tm=0.7`, off by default).
review: Boyan and Chase cameras, close up and at a glitter patch; compare with `?layers=0`.
Sea tab (E): add a Ripples group; try Amount, Gust response and Stretch. Try a 2 km fetch wind sea.
Move the sun (Lighting and surface) and check its shape.
known: The look has not been tuned: the glitter patch is broader and the water slightly darker than before. Presets look different because the wind-sea tail is cut at 1.5 m.
Seen from straight above, the fine detail is subtle.
Tiling can show on a very calm sea. Performance is unmeasured on a quiet machine; a loaded-machine A/B showed no cost increase (the layers replace four value-noise ripple octaves).
